QUESTION:
One of my team has been off for five weeks with a back injury. As her line manager, can I refer her to Occupational Health myself?

CANDIDATE A:
No. OH referrals are made by the HR Advisory team; you can ask HR to make one.

CANDIDATE B:
Yes. Line managers make OH referrals.

RESPONSE:
**A correction first:** my earlier notes were wrong or incomplete in three places that affect your questions. Probationers don't get company sick pay, line managers can't make Occupational Health referrals, and reclaiming annual leave has strict conditions. The answers below come from the policy text itself.

**1. Three months into probation, off sick for a week: will you get full pay?**
No. Under section 4, company sick pay (full pay, then half pay) only applies once you've completed your six-month probation. Until then you get Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) only, and only if you're eligible. The policy doesn't set out SSP rates or eligibility rules, so check those with HR or payroll. Since your absence was a week, you also need to complete the self-certification form on the HR portal (section 3).

**2. Can you, as her line manager, refer your team member to Occupational Health yourself?**
No. Section 6 says referrals are made by the HR Advisory team, not line managers, so that consent and medical confidentiality are handled properly. You can ask HR to make the referral. In any case, at five weeks' continuous absence she has already passed the four-week point at which HR would normally refer. She'll be asked to consent to the OH report being shared with HR and you.

**3. From which day is a fit note required?**
From the **eighth calendar day** of absence onwards (section 3). Absences of up to seven calendar days are self-certified on the HR portal when you return.

**4. Food poisoning on holiday in Portugal: can you reclaim those leave days?**
Almost certainly not. Section 8 lets you reclaim leave days only if you did **both** of these:
- (a) phoned your line manager on the first day of the illness, even while abroad, and
- (b) provided a fit note or, if abroad, a local medical certificate covering the days you were ill.

You didn't do either: you told your manager only when you got back, and you didn't see a doctor. The policy says leave days can't be reclaimed retrospectively without both. Any exception would be at your manager's or HR's discretion, as the policy doesn't provide for one.
